title: A step-commuting map preserves runs
statement: Let $M$ and $M'$ be multi-tape Turing machines, with respectively $k$ and $k'$ work tapes, state sets $S$ and $S'$, and fixed inputs $x$ and $x'$. Suppose a map $f$ sends configurations of $M$ on $x$ to configurations of $M'$ on $x'$ and satisfies $M'.\operatorname{step}(f(c))=f(M.\operatorname{step}(c))$ for every configuration $c$ of $M$. Then for every such configuration $c$ and every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, running $M'$ for $n$ steps from $f(c)$ yields the image under $f$ of the configuration reached by running $M$ for $n$ steps from $c$.
hypotheses_covered: Two multi-tape Turing machines with $k$ and $k'$ work tapes
State sets and fixed inputs for the two machines
A map from configurations of the first machine to configurations of the second
The map commutes with one step on every configuration
A configuration of the first machine
replaced:
Let $M$ and $M'$ be multi-tape Turing machines over the same alphabet, with
$k$ and $k'$ work tapes and running on inputs $x$ and $x'$ respectively, and
let $f$ map configurations of $M$ to configurations of $M'$ so that one step
of $M'$ after $f$ agrees with $f$ after one step of $M$ on every
configuration.  Then for every configuration $c$ of $M$ and every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, running $M'$ for $n$ steps from $f(c)$ yields the image
under $f$ of the configuration $M$ reaches in $n$ steps from $c$.
